title: JPMorgan Estimates Amazon 2027 Capex Will Jump 77% to $395B as Stock Erases Post-Earnings Drop
summary:
JPMorgan estimates Amazon will increase capital expenditures by about 77% to $395 billion in 2027 from roughly $220 billion planned for 2026, following management's guidance that next year's spending will be "meaningfully more." Meanwhile, Amazon shares have rallied 11% from their 7.5% post-earnings drop on Thursday evening, leaving the stock up 3% from its close just before the third quarter report.

On the earnings call, CEO Andy Jassy said Amazon is installing an AI accelerator chip, either a GPU or custom Trainium processor, roughly every 14 seconds as customers consume capacity almost as fast as it comes online. Within Amazon Web Services, Bedrock token volume grew nearly 17-fold year over year, Fortune 500 spending on Bedrock rose almost sevenfold, and inference accounted for well over half of AWS AI revenue.

The stock rebound followed an initial selloff after third quarter revenue of $201.9 billion and earnings of $1.89 per share missed consensus estimates of $202.3 billion and $1.96, while quarterly capital spending hit $77.3 billion and pushed trailing 12 month free cash flow to negative $42.4 billion. Even so, operating income jumped 61% to $28.1 billion as AWS sales rose 39% to $46 billion, and Jassy projected the cloud division will grow more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028.

selectedTweets.bestBit: In those same three months it spent $77.3 billion on data centers and equipment, up from $35 billion a year ago.
selectedTweets.text:
🦔Amazon’s cloud business, AWS, grew 39% last quarter. That’s its fastest growth in years. Earnings missed though. Amazon made $1.89 a share and Wall Street expected about $2. In those same three months it spent $77.3 billion on data centers and equipment, up from $35 billion a year ago.

My Take
I don’t like where Amazon’s cash is going. Over the last 12 months it spent $42 billion more than it brought in, and it has borrowed about $115 billion this year to cover the difference. Jassy says AWS will grow over 40% in each of the next two years, and that’s how he justifies all of it. I’m not so sure. Microsoft and Google pitch investors the same story to defend the same kind of spending (Google borrowed too), and I think at least one of them ends up with way more data centers than customers. I just don’t know which one yet.

Hedgie🤗

$AMZN missed Q3 revenue and EPS estimates after yesterday's close, with a trailing free cash flow outflow of $42.4B.

→ Revenue: $201.9B vs. $202.26B expected, up 12% YoY
→ EPS: $1.89 vs. $1.96 expected
→ AWS: $46.0B, up 39% YoY, its fastest growth in nearly five years
→ Q4 revenue guide: $240.0B to $247.0B, midpoint below the $244.5B expected

On the session, shares are down around 1.7%, recovering from a decline of as much as 7% in extended trading, with Q3 capex at $77.3B against $35.1B a year earlier.

$AMZN operating income rose to $28.1B from $17.4B, with 2026 cash capex held at around $220B.
